findings.text: the added case named for the list-valued parameter compares two documents that do not depend on the value it passes. `mcp_module._crew(action="complete", run_id="run-missing", gate="not-run", commits=[...], dry_run=True)` returns the same document for two commits, for no commits, and for one unrelated commit: probed against the module at the reviewed head, all three answers are `{"dry_run": true, "gate": "not-run", "invocation": "reckon crew complete --run run-missing --gate not-run", "ok": false, "refusal_count": 1, ...}` with the refusal `no live run 'run-missing' ...`, because reckon/crew/promotion.py:663 `_dry_run_invocation` composes the invocation from the refusals and never prints a commit. The assertion therefore holds whatever the tool does with `commits` — dropping the argument, passing a bare string, or passing the wrong list all leave `tool == cli` true, so the parity case does not guard the transport it is named for. What it does guard: that the two surfaces agree on the refusal itself.

the rendering is whole-or-none for the option NAMES, not for the values: the value is interpolated into a double-quoted string with no escaping, so `reckon crew complete --run run-x --gate passed --outcome 'say "hi" now'` renders `crew(action="complete", run_id="run-x", gate="passed", outcome="say "hi" now")` — not a callable form, which is the property the repair exists to give the field, and unlike an unmapped option it is not refused. Verified by running the reviewed `action_form` on that command. Not reachable today: every command the classifier composes for a `complete` or `land` duty carries only `<...>` placeholders and commit shas (reckon/crew/recovery_classification.py:1652-1661), so no live duty renders a quoted value — the hole is latent rather than live.
